Approved Requirement (Foundation Plan V1: Document, page and passage-level citations plus evidence status.

Page-level citation is impossible: page numbers are discarded at extraction. Evidence status does not exist.

Recommended Next Action: Preserve page boundaries in the extractor and add document_chunks.page_start/page_end. Contained change with high proof value.

Approved Requirement (Foundation Plan V1: Retrieval grounded only in permitted evidence with citation and confidence.
Acceptance Test (Foundation Plan V1.0): Unsupported approved claims equal zero in evaluation sample.
Existing Implementation: This is the strongest AI control in the repository. Retrieval is hard-scoped to the caller's organization_id in SQL; the model sees only opaque SOURCE_n keys; the service rejects any response citing a key outside the assembled context; a minimum relevance threshold pre-filters context; an explicit insufficient-evidence path exists; overall_confidence is captured.
Evidence Found: rag_analysis.py:362-368 marks a run FAILED if the model cites an unknown source key — a real, tested anti-fabrication control. However structured_output.py:68-70 requires source_keys only on reported_metrics, key_findings and recommendations; executive_summary, detected_topics and overall_confidence carry NO citation requirement.
Gap: (1) executive_summary is free text with zero citation obligation — an unsupported narrative claim can be returned and is currently unpreventable. (2) overall_confidence is self-reported by the model and uncalibrated. (3) No evaluation set and no evaluation harness exist, so the acceptance test ('zero unsupported approved claims in an evaluation sample') has never been executed. (4) No prompt-injection defence: document text is interpolated directly into the user prompt (prompts.py:50), so a hostile PDF can address the model. (5) No approval step exists, so 'approved claims' is currently undefined.
Risk: HIGH. The control design is good but its acceptance test is unexecuted, and the single most-read field of the output — the executive summary — is the one field with no grounding requirement.
Recommended Next Action: Add a citation obligation (or an explicit 'derived, uncited' marking) to executive_summary; build a fixed evaluation set with normal/ambiguous/conflicting/malicious inputs per Plan §5.1; add prompt-injection delimiting and a hostile-document test case.

Approved Requirement (Foundation Plan V1: Authentication; least-privilege roles and record/project access enforcement on server.

Exact Source Files: backend/app/infrastructure/security/supabase_jwt.py:49-157; backend/app/api/deps.py:121-137; backend/app/services/organization.py:36-75; backend/app/services/engagement.py; backend/app/services/document_read.py; backend/app/services/analysis/rag_analysis.py:169-218; backend/app/infrastructure/storage/supabase_document_storage.py:21-23 (service-role key bypasses RLS)

Evidence Found: Cross-tenant probes deliberately return 404 rather than 403 so a foreign id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one (organization.py:70-74) — a correct, deliberate control, and negatively tested. No migration in backend/migrations/versions contains CREATE POLICY or ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
Gap: (1) Zero server-side role enforcement — users.role is read only to echo it back at auth.py:31. (2) No RLS defence-in-depth; a single missed service-layer check has no second barrier. Recommended Next Action: SPRINT 1 PRIORITY 1: server-side role enforcement dependency + per-endpoint permission map + negative tests per role; then RLS policies as defence-in-depth.
